name: Mefenamic acid
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Mefenamic acid is a fenamate nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) whose metabolites are excreted mainly in urine and can accumulate. The US label says it should not be given to patients with pre-existing kidney disease or significantly impaired kidney function. NSAID kidney risks (acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, fluid retention) apply. For pain the label limits use to 1 week.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses qualitative terms (pre-existing renal disease, significantly impaired renal function); no CrCl threshold. Band mapping is our judgment.

bands.recommendation: 500 mg first dose, then 250 mg every 6 hours as needed; usually not beyond 1 week (label). Check kidney function before use if risk factors.

Label 8.6: should not be given to patients with pre-existing kidney disease or significantly impaired kidney function; metabolites (excreted mainly in urine) may accumulate. Not studied in kidney impairment.
bands.short: Avoid: label says not in CKD

hd.text: Avoid (label: not in pre-existing kidney disease). Not dialyzable (high protein binding). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Avoid (label: not in pre-existing kidney disease). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury.

dialyzable: Unlikely: hemodialysis may not be useful because of high protein binding (label 10).
monitoring: Kidney function before and during use in at-risk patients; stop if kidney function worsens. Potassium, blood pressure; gastrointestinal bleeding.

pediatric.approved_ages: Pain: 14 years and older. Primary dysmenorrhea: established in pediatric patients (label 8.4).
pediatric.usual_dose: 14 years and older: 500 mg, then 250 mg every 6 hours as needed (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Not stated as mg/kg; usually no more than 1 week.

renal.recommendation: Avoid: label says not in pre-existing kidney disease (not limited by age).
renal.short: Avoid: label says not in CKD

adult: JUDGMENT: label 8.6 wording ('should not be administered to patients with pre-existing renal disease') makes the CrCl 30–59 tile red. Dr. Rivero may prefer amber (caution) for mild CKD.
US product is 250 mg capsules only; PH sells mainly 500 mg capsules and tablets, plus 250 mg and 50 mg/5 mL suspension. The 500 mg first dose equals one PH 500 mg capsule.
Label 5.5 also says 'avoid in advanced renal disease unless benefits outweigh the risk' (class wording), which is softer than 8.6.
